body.statement: If \(b\le2\), then \(\operatorname{Fail}(S)=1\) if and only if there is \(\beta=(x,r,e^{\to},e^{\leftrightarrow})\in\mathcal B\) whose two edges lie in \(E^{\mathrm{det}}\cup S\) and for which \(r\) reaches \(Y\) in the directed part of \(G_S[V\setminus X]\). Moreover, \(\mathcal O_{XY}\) is exactly the family of inclusion-minimal label unions \(L(P)\) of \(\sigma\)-to-\(t\) paths in \(T^{\mathrm{proj}}\). The child rule in Definition~\ref{def:width-two-projection}, retaining only the \(\prec\)-least chordless representative of each label union and testing label-union minimality by reachability, enumerates every member exactly once with polynomial preprocessing, worst-case delay, exhaustion time, and space. For a fixed label union, the ordered singleton-labelled internal vertices are unique and at most \(|\mathcal B|\) bow vertices can supply candidate representatives.
body.justification: Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) supplies the original-query hedge equivalence; the theorem specializes its certificates at district size two and validates a complete projection algorithm without the unresolved multiple-root recursion.
body.gap: The original-query criterion in Shpitser (2023, Proposition 1) is not an enumeration result, while directed-path and Steiner enumeration do not suppress the exponential multiplicity of deterministic path witnesses or collisions between bow starts that yield the same uncertain support.
body.consumer: It gives an immediately implementable exact compiler for uncertain envelopes with only pairwise latent-confounding districts.
